name: What follows from a reaction, so nothing he said waits unanswered
when: a reaction has landed on the Brief (a distinction found, a text arrived, a memo found, a verdict changed, a question answered) and the desk must decide the next step without being asked (the owner, 2026-09-07 13:55: automate the follow-up so he thinks rather than checks and remembers)
shape: distinction_found → file the questions back on the part; when he answers, run distinction_settle with the answer and the parts, file S1 as a proposed edit with the interlocutor cited, S2 as effects, S3 as open · text_arrived for a hunch or a reference → re-run the pass that waited on it (a hunch test, a re-read) and say on the row which hunch it feeds · memo_found → the next re-read or distinction round carries it as an analysis source under a recollection statement · verdict_changed (a hunch, a frame) → re-ask the frame (what would change this verdict) and mark the parts that rested on the old verdict downstream · question_back answered → the reading that asked it runs again with the answer; an unanswered question older than a day is reminded once, never nagged · reread_done → the references that hold become citations on the part, those that diverge become challenges · blocked → name what it waits on (a text, a slot, his approval of a desk-draft part) and who acts
ingredients: the trigger with his sentence quoted
the reach from structure (local · downstream · premise)
the day's ceiling of unsolicited interventions
yields: the chain trigger → reaction → changed → could change → next on every row, and a reminder strip for the ideas he voiced when material for them lands
misses: a follow-up that needs a text nobody holds (it stays blocked, named); a change whose reach the structure cannot see (a distinction's reach comes from the reading: challenges[].bears_on)
origin: the Stacks' code does each of these already (2026-09-07); the record makes them one rule an LLM can revise
note: Read by the Stacks and the Mastermind alike; cite it on the row's `next`.
